item.text:
**Overall**
Mostly no direct evidence of patronage use. Kishida’s 2024 welfare and relief measures were generally framed as universal, needs-based, or rule-bound, with explicit transparency and budget discipline. The clearest negative signal I found was tougher migration control, but that is not the same as using welfare, jobs, housing, or permits as loyalty rewards or punishments.

**Positive**
- **Policy Speech by Prime Minister Kishida to the 213th Session of the Diet** | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | January 30, 2024 | https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202401/30shiseihoshin.html | Kishida said child policy would be expanded on an unprecedented scale and funded through expenditure reform rather than added household burden, which points to programmatic social provision rather than loyalty-based distribution. | QIDs: `6B.7`, `6B.4`, `6B.5`, `6B.2`
- **Policies supporting children and child-rearing** | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | 2024 page content | https://japan.kantei.go.jp/ongoingtopics/policies_kishida/childsupport.html | The child-allowance program is described as universal and income-independent, with fixed monthly payments for all eligible households, which is strong evidence against using benefits as a political reward system. | QIDs: `6B.7`, `6B.2`, `6B.4`, `6B.5`
- **Press Conference by Prime Minister Kishida** | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | June 21, 2024 | https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202406/21kaiken.html | Kishida said expanded local-government subsidies would cushion school lunches, agriculture, SMEs, care services, childcare, transport, logistics, and low-income households, with special support tied to price shocks rather than political loyalty. | QIDs: `6B.7`, `6B.4`, `6B.5`, `6B.2`, `6B.3`
- **Press Conference by Prime Minister Kishida on His Visit to Ishikawa Prefecture to Confirm the Extent of the Damage Caused by the 2024 Noto Peninsula Earthquake and Other Matters** | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | February 24, 2024 | https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202402/24kaiken.html | Kishida described aid eligibility broadly, including households with children, low-income households, and households with damaged homes, and said support would be delivered through simple, prompt procedures. | QIDs: `6B.7`, `6B.6`, `6B.4`
- **Meeting of the Council on Economic and Fiscal Policy** | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | July 29, 2024 | https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/actions/202407/29keizai.html | Kishida explicitly said the government would use medium- and long-term projections, spending reform, and EBPM to improve policy effectiveness, which is the opposite of patronage allocation. | QIDs: `6B.7`, `6B.5`, `5B.10`, `6B.4`
- **Prime Minister’s Office of Japan press conference on the Noto response** | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | January 5, 2024 | https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202401/05kaiken.html | The Noto relief package focused on rescue, reopening transport, and restoring daily life and livelihoods, with no sign of selective punishment or loyalty screening. | QIDs: `6B.7`, `6B.6`, `6B.4`

**Mixed / Negative**
- **岸田文雄のウソ？ホント？** | Kishida Fumio official website / LDP-affiliated site | 2024 page content | https://kishida.gr.jp/fact/ | The “illegal foreigners zero” section describes tighter entry screening, deportation enforcement, and stricter refugee procedures, which is the clearest 2024 case of administrative exclusion, though it is not direct proof of welfare or jobs being used as political punishment. | QIDs: `6B.7`, `6B.3`, `6B.5`
- **Embattled Japan PM faces ethics committee to save popularity and budget** | Reuters | February 28, 2024 | https://www.investing.com/news/economy/embattled-japan-pm-faces-ethics-committee-to-save-popularity-and-budget-3319362 | Reuters reported Kishida was pulled into defensive politics by the funding scandal, which suggests political survival pressure shaped the agenda, but it does not show him using welfare or permits as a loyalty tool. | QIDs: `6B.7`, `6B.5`, `5B.5`
- **Japan PM Kishida won’t run for reelection at LDP race, Kyodo reports** | Reuters | August 14, 2024 | https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/japan-pm-kishida-wont-run-for-reelection-at-ldp-race-kyodo-reports-3570455 | Reuters framed his exit as a response to scandals and living-cost anger; again, this indicates political weakness and coalition management, not direct patronage via welfare or housing. | QIDs: `6B.7`, `5B.5`, `5B.10`

**Search gap**
- I did **not** find credible 2024 evidence that Kishida withheld child benefits, housing, disaster aid, public jobs, or permits from opponents, or handed them out as explicit loyalty rewards.
- The record instead points to broadly framed subsidies, universal child support, and disaster relief routed through formal institutions.
- The main ambiguous area is migration policy: the tougher “illegal foreigners zero” line is exclusionary, but it still looks more like administrative control than a patronage system.
